_comment: Golden vectors for the billing-period rule — the ONE rule that exists twice:
deriveBillingPeriod() in src/lib/billing.ts (TypeScript). Both files say the
rule has caused real production bugs when re-derived from scratch, and they
are kept in step by discipline alone. These vectors replace the discipline.
THE RULE: a non-Sunset bill arriving ON OR BEFORE the 10th bills to the
PREVIOUS month (the 10th is INCLUSIVE, matching the Companion's 10th-to-10th
invoicing window); after the 10th it bills to the arrival month. Sunset bills
ALWAYS bill in their arrival month.
`receivedUtc` is a UTC instant, not a calendar date, on purpose: the rule is
evaluated in America/Los_Angeles, so a bill uploaded at 11pm Pacific on the
10th must NOT count as the 11th. Several vectors below sit either side of
that boundary and would fail any implementation that used UTC dates.
Edit THIS file, then re-run the generator and commit both.

vectors.name: non-Sunset, 1st → previous month
non-Sunset, 10th is INCLUSIVE → previous month
non-Sunset, 11th → arrival month
TZ boundary: 11pm Pacific on the 10th is still the 10th
TZ boundary: 1am Pacific on the 11th is the 11th
non-Sunset, January 5th → December of the PREVIOUS year
non-Sunset, January 10th → December, year rolls back
TZ + year rollover: 11pm Pacific Jan 10 → December 2025
TZ + year rollover: 1am Pacific Jan 11 → January 2026
non-Sunset, December 31st → December (no roll forward)
non-Sunset, March 1st → February
non-Sunset, leap-year Feb 29 (after the 10th) → February
Sunset, 5th → arrival month, NOT the previous one
Sunset, 10th → arrival month (the 10th rule does not apply)
Sunset, 11th → arrival month
Sunset, January 3rd → January, no year rollback
Sunset, TZ boundary 11pm Pacific Jan 10 → January
non-Sunset, mid-month → arrival month
non-Sunset, last day of a 30-day month → that month
non-Sunset, February 10th → January
